answer: To prevent sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce a work requirement that chains previous activities, making it costly for an attacker to create new identities. Each new identity must build on the previous one, creating a verifiable trail. In a meadow of legitimate agents, a bridge of trust is formed by requiring each agent to demonstrate a consistent work history, similar to tending an orchard where each tree has a unique growth pattern. An attacker trying to create multiple identities would have to replicate this history for each one, increasing their cost and making it harder to launch
